To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ACE inhibitor captopril causes an acute decrease in blood pressure and renal vascular resistance in anesthetized dogs that is associated with an increase of renal blood flow and a decrease in glomerular filtration rate.

ACE inhibition increases intra-renal kinin levels and that decreased degradation by these tissue vasodilation peptides may contribute significantly in the acute renal vasodialtion and hypotensive effects of captopril.
ACE inhibition leads to an increase in intra-renal kinin levels which contribute to the acute renal hemodynamic response to ACE inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of captopriol (ACE inhibitor) on the kidney.
the effects of captopril on renal blood flow and the kallikreinkinin system.
the effects of angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors on renal blood flow and renal kinins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acute effects of ACE inhibitors are not mediated by angiotensin.
captopril causes renal vasodilation, which is mediated in part by increased levels of intra- renal kinins.
the acute renal hemodynamic effects of ACE inhibition are not due to a decrease in AII but are mediated, at least in part, by increased intra-renal levels of kinins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ACE inhibition leads to a significant increase in intra-renal kallikreins and kinins.
captopril increases renal blood flow, glomerular filtration rate, and renal excretion of sodium and potassium.
ACE inhibition increases the level of kinins in the kidneys.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ACE inhibition increases the levels of kinins, which are tissue vasodilators and that decreased degradation may contribute significantly to acute renal vasodilator and hypotensive effects of captopril.

the renin- angiotensin system is involved in the regulation of the renal kallkrein-kinin and prostaglandin systems and that these two systems interact with the renin-angiostensin system to maintain renal function.
ACE inhibition leads to an increase in kinin levels, which in turn leads to renal vasodilation.
